patterns.description: All three CCPA Regulatory Website Updates workstreams (Dealer Systems, Web Platform, Mobile) depend on the same legal team deliverable: the CCPA copy. Mobile and Web Platform have already completed their implementation work, but Dealer Systems is explicitly blocked because legal has not yet provided the required copy, and it's unclear if Web Platform's 'copy implemented' means it received different/partial copy or is now stale pending legal finalization.
patterns.why_it_matters: The program lead should escalate directly to the legal team this week to unblock CRH-4 before the Aug 14 due date, and confirm with Web Platform (CRH-2) whether the copy they implemented is the final legal-approved version, since a single legal bottleneck is now the critical path for the entire CCPA initiative despite two of three teams reporting on_track.

patterns.description: Three separate tickets across different teams and initiatives (Dealer Portal Release Calendar, Consent Taxonomy Review, CCPA Dealer Systems) are all blocked due to unowned_escalation signals -- unanswered requests, a traveling VP with no delegate for sign-off, and legal not delivering copy with no one driving urgency. In each case, no one is actively pushing the blocking party to respond.
patterns.why_it_matters: This is a pattern of stalled decisions/approvals with no escalation ownership across multiple unrelated teams. The program lead should establish an explicit escalation path (e.g., designate approval delegates for traveling execs, set SLAs for legal/vendor responses) rather than treating each as an isolated one-off blocker.

patterns.description: Both CRH-10 (Consent Signal Integration) and CRH-11 (Partner Integration Incident Response) involve inter-team dependencies where one side had to wait on another to respond (Signal team agreeing to a new date; partner providing details) before work could proceed, both resulting in due date slips within days of each other (Aug 14-15).
patterns.why_it_matters: While each is individually manageable, the clustering of slipped due dates tied to external/partner response times suggests the program lead should review whether response-time SLAs with partners and cross-team signal dependencies need tightening to avoid a pattern of recurring date slips.
